subject.title: [Bug]: ACP binding session generates new acp_session_id after gateway restart, causing resume failure with misleading 'model not found' error

question: When a persistent ACP binding cannot resume its stored backend transcript after restart, should OpenClaw preserve-first then automatically recreate, always fail for explicit recovery, or always start fresh?
rationale: The choice determines whether OpenClaw favors transcript continuity, automatic availability, or explicit operator control, and it must remain consistent across restart, `/reset`, and `/acp close`.

options.title: Preserve, then recover
options.body: Reuse the persisted identity first, but atomically recreate and clearly notify the user when the backend confirms that the transcript is missing.

options.title: Fail explicitly
options.body: Preserve transcript continuity strictly and require an in-product Fix/Doctor action before creating a replacement session.

options.title: Always start fresh
options.body: Discard persisted backend identity after every gateway restart, accepting conversation-history loss for simpler recovery.

recommendation.title: Preserve, then recover
recommendation.body: Reuse the persisted identity first, but atomically recreate and clearly notify the user when the backend confirms that the transcript is missing.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the persistent binding and adjacent Telegram ACP lifecycle implementations, providing the strongest available ownership signal.
